text: I see you are experiencing jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine. Have you noticed any abdominal pain or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of gallstones or prior episodes of biliary colic, and have you experienced any recent episodes of fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless jaundice and significant weight loss in a heavy smoker, I suspect pancreatic cancer. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan was normal, we need to rule out other causes of biliary obstruction. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP reveals a dilated common bile duct with a smooth, tapered distal obstruction. No filling defects or masses are visualized within the pancreatic head or ampulla of Vater. The intrahepatic bile ducts are also dilated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging findings of a smooth, tapered distal obstruction without a visible mass are classic for IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis, especially given the absence of alcohol use. REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgG4_level

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated IgG4 levels combined with the characteristic imaging findings confirm IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
